text:
alisa: Quick follow-up from the requantifier RFC — i'm worried our transition strategy (instant switch -> fallback) is causing micro-regressions on multi-turn tasks. noticed on a customer shadow run where fp8->int8 flip produced stuttered logits across turn boundaries. anyone else seen this?
matt: saw similar in perf tests. looks like KV cache scaling + per-layer requant causes small distribution shifts, then topk moves.
sandeep: that matches the hypothesis — abrupt precision changes can perturb normalization layers and attention scale. we should consider a staged attenuation rather than atomic switch.
rachel: agree. proposal: a sliding requant window that blends outputs for N tokens during transition. basically linear interpolation on activations or outputs for the first M tokens post-switch. cheap and reversible.
alisa: interpolation sounds promising but we need clear operators in runtime. do we do it at activation tensors (requires operator support) or at logits level (safer but potentially less precise)?
ben: logits-level blending is easiest: keep last-known logits from previous precision and linearly mix with current logits for T steps. pseudocode:```python
for t in range(T):
    mix = 1 - t/(T-1)
    out[t] = mix * logits_old[t] + (1-mix) * logits_new[t]
```
drawback: it mixes final distribution rather than internal state, may mask internal instabilities.
sandeep: activation-level would preserve hidden-state continuity but requires kernel support and KV cache awareness. also need to ensure mixed KV entries are consistent.
ops-bot: reminder: any runtime kernel changes must go through eng-runtime CI and perf gating. See https://go/redwood-eng-runtime-cq for checklist.
rachel: alternative hybrid: do a quick per-layer scale correction before switch — compute layerwise mean/std diff on a tiny calibration window, apply affine correction to activations when switching. cheaper than full activation blend and avoids logits mixing.
matt: calibration sounds nice if it's cheap. we can reuse shadow traffic samples (first N tokens of trace) to estimate shifts. need to pick N small (like 32-128 tokens).
alisa: operationally: we need config knobs per-customer: 1) switch-mode: instant|logit-blend|activation-calib 2) blend-steps: int 3) calib-window: int 4) hysteresis-ms: int. default should be activation-calib with hysteresis to prevent flapping.\enote: example route config snippet:```yaml
precision_transition:
  mode: activation-calib
  calib_window_tokens: 64
  blend_steps: 16
  hysteresis_ms: 2000
```
ben: also track metrics: per-turn perplexity delta, ngram-fidelity, and rollout-degscore. emit an event when delta exceeds threshold so ops can rollback.
sandeep: important: ensure fallback policy backs out quant change if post-switch degscore > threshold for M consecutive requests (not just one). prevents noisy single-query triggers.
matt: can we lightweight simulate the switch offline? like run fp8 and int8 shadow on same inputs and precompute expected delta to decide route-level policy automatically.
alisa: yes that's part of optimize plans. but for rapid rollout we need runtime safety: cheap activation-calib + per-route hysteresis + consecutive-failures backoff.
rachel: one more edge-case: long-context caching. if we switch mid-session, older KV entries are in previous precision; mixing strategies must account for that or we should only switch between user sessions.\enote: idea: disallow mid-session precision upgrades; allow mid-session downgrades (safer) and schedule upgrades at session boundary. that reduces complexity.
b: +1 to session-boundary-only upgrades. less complexity and safer for customers with stateful prompts.
ben: OK i'll draft a short ops playbook and a runtime API patch: /v1/models/{id}/precision_transition [PATCH] with fields above. also add telemetry hooks.
alisa: thanks — matt/sandeep/rachel can you +1 on the approach in the next 48h? i'll fold into the RFC follow-up and add canary checklist.
matt: +1 from me.
sandeep: +1, but would like to run a quick microbench for activation-calib perf impact.
rachel: +1, will prototype a logit-blend fallback for comparison.
alisa: great — schedule quick sync if needed. :thumbsup:
